title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Hyperbola Detection in GPR B-Scans for Routine Utility Survey Processing

record.title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Hyperbola Detection in GPR B-Scans for Routine Utility Survey Processing
record.abstract: Manual interpretation of GPR B-scans is time-consuming and operator-dependent, particularly for large-scale cadastre surveys producing hundreds of radargrams per day. This study trained and tested a convolutional neural network to detect hyperbolic reflections indicative of buried point and linear targets in B-scans collected with 500 MHz and 250 MHz antennas over urban streets in Novi Sad. A labelled dataset of 8,400 B-scan images with 22,310 annotated hyperbolas was assembled from three years of field surveys. The network achieved precision of 0.87 and recall of 0.84 on a held-out test set, outperforming a matched-filter baseline (precision 0.73, recall 0.71). False positive rate was highest for tree root reflections and reinforced concrete slab edges. Integration into a semi-automatic processing pipeline reduced per-radargram interpretation time from an average of 4.2 minutes to 1.1 minutes, with human expert review retained for flagged ambiguous cases. The labelled dataset is made available for benchmarking.
